review.tagline: Embedding database with a four-function API for Python and JavaScript
review.summary: Chroma is an embedding database with a four-function API (create collection, add, query, get) that tokenizes, embeds and indexes documents itself or accepts your own vectors, with metadata and document filters. It runs in-memory or persisted from the Python or JavaScript client, or as a server via chroma run; the repo ships a Dockerfile and compose file. Chroma Cloud is the hosted serverless version.
review.audience: developers prototyping RAG who want the simplest API
strengths: Four-function API: create collection, add, query, get
Handles tokenization, embedding and indexing; own vectors optional
Python and JavaScript clients; chroma run for client-server mode
Weekly tagged releases on Mondays with hotfixes in between
weaknesses: README is thin: no port, resource or auth guidance
Hosted Chroma Cloud is the headline; self-hosting detail lives in docs
No multi-user auth described in the README
needs: Models: built-in embedding or user-supplied vectors
